channel.title: Gnarly Void - pokemon
channel.description: Tufted fiber art, weaving, pottery, and handmade objects by Jake Goldsborough in the Pacific Northwest.

item.title: Shocked Pikachu
item.author: site@gnarlyvoid.com (Jake Goldsborough)
item.description:
The shocked Pikachu meme, as a rug.

The whole face is one flat field of yellow, cut to the silhouette so the ears reach up and out past any frame. There is almost nothing inside it: two round black eyes, a dot of a nose, a small pink mouth held open, and the red cheeks sitting low and wide. The black ear tips and the heavy contour around the outside are the only other marks.

Everything hinges on the eyes. Each one carries a single white loop, set slightly off center, and that off-center placement is the entire expression. Move it a few tufts and the face is calm. Where it is now, the face is caught.

The pile keeps the yellow uneven enough that it does not read as a print, and the mouth and cheeks pick up a little shadow along their edges where the color changes. The cut edge is where the tufting shows most, with the black backing outline pulled a little rough around the ears.

It is a joke that has been repeated a few million times, made slowly by hand out of yarn. That is probably the funniest version of it.

item.title: Lugia
item.author: site@gnarlyvoid.com (Jake Goldsborough)
item.description:
Lugia, suspended between flight and the wall.

The wings take up almost the whole frame, broad and slightly uneven as if the creature has just pulled them in. The head and neck sit low between them, with the long tail curling down and back into the body. White, grey, and purple separate the planes without turning the image into a flat stack of color; the black outline gives every feathered shape somewhere to stop.

The useful tension is between the subject's weight and its posture. This is a large, dense rug, but Lugia is drawn as if it should be moving through air. The tufted loops catch the light differently across each section, so the wings read as volume while the heavy contour keeps the silhouette immediate from across the room. The white catches the light first, the greys settle the middle, and the purples give the shadows somewhere to deepen.

The work stays recognizable as a Pokémon illustration, but the material changes the speed of it. Flight becomes something thick, soft, and fixed in place.
